simple.meaning: רָחוֹק (râchôwq) is a Hebrew concept word meaning “remote , literally or figuratively, of place or time; specifically, precious ; often used adverbially (with preposition).” BibleIQ follows how Scripture develops this idea across its occurrences.
simple.biblicalBackground: The concept appears 85 times across Genesis, Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, and 22 more, beginning at Genesis 22:4. Its contexts include family, kingship, mountain, Israel.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to רָחוֹק (H7350).
simple.whyItMatters: Concept words shape biblical themes. BibleIQ keeps the concept grounded in actual verse evidence instead of starting with a later theological definition.
simple.summary: רָחוֹק (râchôwq) / H7350 is traced through Genesis 22:4, Genesis 37:18, Exodus 2:4, Exodus 20:18 as a generated source-based concept entry.
